mainTopic: A man who married his wife's sister after a false report of his wife's death: the status of his wife, the sister and the children, and whether this fits רבי עקיבא's view
overview: This amud finishes the משנה about a man who was told his wife had died and then married her sister. The משנה rules that his real wife may go back to him, that the mistaken marriage creates no family ties, and that a child born from the sister while the wife was still alive is a ממזר. רבי יוסי adds a short rule about disqualifying others and oneself, which the גמרא explains later. The גמרא adds that even when the sister was herself married and becomes forbidden to her own husband, the man's own wife stays permitted. It then asks whether this fits רבי עקיבא, who requires a גט for a wife's sister. The answer is that רבי עקיבא only meant a case where the first wife was just betrothed, since nobody assumes a full marriage had a condition. רב אשי asks why רבי עקיבא's list leaves out the mother-in-law. רב כהנא answers that removing the punishment of burning does not remove the איסור. Finally the גמרא asks why the wife isn't forbidden through her husband's relations with her sister, and it begins to explain why this differs from the case of a woman whose husband went overseas.

steps.title: The false marriage creates no family ties
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes its ruling. His real wife may return to him. The second woman and his relatives are not connected at all, and if his wife dies he may marry the second woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: [His first wife is permitted to return] to him. He may marry the relatives of the second woman, and the second woman may marry his relatives. And if the first woman dies, he may marry the second woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is finishing its first case and listing what happens after the false marriage to the wife's sister.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His marriage to the sister never took effect, because she is his wife's sister. So it creates no in-law ties in either direction. Once his wife dies, the sister is no longer forbidden to him, so he may marry her.

keyTerms.meaning: female relatives
the second woman (here, the wife's sister he wrongly married)
the first woman, his real wife
permitted

phrases.english: to him.
phrases.notes: This is the end of the משנה's sentence from the last page: his first wife is permitted to go back to him.

phrases.english: And he is permitted to the relatives of the second woman,
and the second woman is permitted to his relatives.
And if the first woman died —
he is permitted to the second.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A marriage to the wife's sister made by mistake has no legal effect. It creates no in-law prohibitions, and after the wife dies he may marry the sister.

steps.title: Which child is a ממזר
steps.stepSummary: He was told his wife died, so he married her sister. Later it turned out his wife had still been alive and only died afterward. A child born while the wife was alive is a ממזר; a child born after her death is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: They told him his wife died, and he married her sister. Afterward they told him she had been alive at the time and died later. The first child is a ממזר, and the later child is not a ממזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a new case where the wife really did die, but only after he had already married her sister.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While his wife was alive, being with her sister was a forbidden relationship, so a child from that time is a ממזר. After the wife died, the sister was no longer forbidden to him, so a child born then is not a ממזר. The timing of the wife's death decides it.

keyTerms.meaning: a child born from a forbidden relationship, who may not marry into the regular community
alive, still living
child
her sister

phrases.english: They said to him: his wife died,
and he married her sister.
And afterward they said to him:
She was alive, and then died.
The first child is a ממזר,
and the last one is not a ממזר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new case in the same משנה: this time the wife's death is real but happened later.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A child born from the wife's sister while the wife was alive is a ממזר. A child born after the wife's death is not.
steps.whatToRemember: What decides whether the child is a ממזר is whether the wife was alive when the child came from her sister.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's rule about disqualifying
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי gives a short general rule: whoever disqualifies others also disqualifies himself, and whoever does not disqualify others does not disqualify himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: Whoever disqualifies through others disqualifies through himself, and whoever does not disqualify through others does not disqualify through himself.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי adds a short, puzzling rule to the משנה. The גמרא will explain what it means later on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule says that disqualifying through others and disqualifying through oneself go together: either both happen or neither does. The משנה does not say who or what is being disqualified, so don't try to work it out yet. Wait for the גמרא to explain it.

keyTerms.meaning: a תנא who adds his own view here
disqualifies, makes someone unfit
through others
through himself

steps.confusionAlert: The meaning of רבי יוסי's rule is not clear from the משנה alone. Don't force a meaning onto it now; the גמרא explains it later.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
Whoever disqualifies through others —
disqualifies through himself,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל שֶׁאֵין פּוֹסֵל עַל יְדֵי אֲחֵרִים —
phrases.english: and whoever does not disqualify through others —
does not disqualify through himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: כׇּל שֶׁפּוֹסֵל עַל יְדֵי אֲחֵרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A separate opinion added at the end of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Disqualifying through others and disqualifying through oneself go together: either both apply or neither does.

steps.title: The married sister becomes forbidden, but his wife stays permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds a case. His wife and her sister's husband both went overseas, and he married the sister. That marriage does forbid the sister to her own husband. Even so, his own wife stays permitted to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even if his wife and his brother-in-law went overseas, so this marriage does have an effect, because his brother-in-law's wife becomes forbidden to his brother-in-law, even so: his brother-in-law's wife is forbidden, but his own wife is permitted. We do not say: since his brother-in-law's wife became forbidden to his brother-in-law, his own wife should be forbidden to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא comments on the משנה with a harder case: the sister he married was herself a married woman whose husband was also thought to be dead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the mistaken marriage does have a result: the sister becomes forbidden to her real husband. You might think the man's own marriage would also be harmed, so his wife would become forbidden to him. The גמרא says no: only the sister is forbidden to her husband, and his wife stays permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: his brother-in-law (here, the husband of his wife's sister)
overseas, a faraway land
had an effect
forbidden / permitted
since, because of the fact that

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ וְאַף עַל גַּב דַּאֲזוּל אִשְׁתּוֹ וְגִיסוֹ לִמְדִינַת הַיָּם,
phrases.english: GEMARA: And even though his wife and his brother-in-law went overseas,
so that this marriage is effective
in that his brother-in-law's wife becomes forbidden to his brother-in-law,
even so:
his brother-in-law's wife is forbidden, his own wife is permitted,
and we do not say:
since his brother-in-law's wife became forbidden to his brother-in-law,
his own wife should be forbidden to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל גַּב דַּאֲזוּל אִשְׁתּוֹ וְגִיסוֹ לִמְדִינַת הַיָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the משנה's first case and adds a version where the sister was married.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even when the mistaken marriage forbids the sister to her own husband, the man's own wife remains permitted to him.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling is what the next step questions: can it fit with רבי עקיבא?

steps.title: Does the משנה go against רבי עקיבא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the משנה does not follow רבי עקיבא. According to him, the man's wife would now count as the sister of his divorcée.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that the משנה is not following רבי עקיבא? Because if it followed רבי עקיבא, his wife would be the sister of his divorcée.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests that the ruling 'his wife stays permitted' cannot match רבי עקיבא's view. This sets up a discussion that will continue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי עקיבא, the sister he married would count as his divorcée. That would make his own wife 'the sister of his divorcée.' The גמרא assumes that status would cause a problem for his wife. That clashes with the ruling just given that his wife stays permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: shall we say? (a suggestion the גמרא tests)
a תנא whose view is being compared to the משנה
the sister of his divorcée

phrases.english: Shall we say that our משנה
is not like Rabbi Akiva,
for if it were Rabbi Akiva —
she would be the sister of his divorcée.
phrases.notes: 'She' is his own wife. The sister he wrongly married would count as his divorcée.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the ruling of step 4 against רבי עקיבא's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the man's own wife stays permitted to him
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רבי עקיבא, the sister counts as his divorcée, which makes his wife 'the sister of his divorcée.' That seems to clash with saying she stays permitted, so the משנה would not follow רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: The ברייתא that shows רבי עקיבא's view
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the עריות do not need a גט, except an אשת איש who remarried by בית דין's permission. רבי עקיבא adds an אשת אח and an אחות אשה. So by רבי עקיבא, the sister needs a גט, and the real wife becomes the sister of his divorcée.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: none of the women forbidden as עריות need a גט from him, except a married woman who remarried with בית דין's permission. רבי עקיבא adds a brother's wife and a wife's sister. Since רבי עקיבא says the sister needs a גט, the wife automatically becomes forbidden to him, because she is now his divorcée's sister.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as proof for its claim from the last step, that our משנה does not follow רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, marrying one of the עריות means nothing, so no גט is needed. רבי עקיבא requires a גט for an אחות אשה. Once he gives her a גט, his real wife counts as 'the sister of his divorcée,' who is forbidden to him. That clashes with our משנה, which lets the wife go back to him.

keyTerms.meaning: Relationships the Torah forbids, such as close relatives or a married woman
A bill of divorce
With the permission of the court
Automatically, by itself
The sister of his divorcée, who is forbidden to him

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי עקיבא holds that the marriage to the sister actually worked. It did not work. He only requires a גט, and that גט is what creates the 'divorcée's sister' problem.

phrases.english: As it is taught: all forbidden relations in the Torah
do not need a bill of divorce from him,
except a married woman
who remarried by the court's permission,
and Rabbi Akiva adds
also a brother's wife and a wife's sister.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵיוָן דְּאָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא בָּעֲיָא גֵּט,
phrases.english: And since Rabbi Akiva said she needs a bill of divorce,
phrases.notes: 'She' here is the wife's sister, whom the man married by mistake.

phrases.english: automatically [his wife] becomes forbidden to him,
since she is the sister of his divorcée.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for step 5's claim that the משנה does not follow רבי עקיבא.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that our משנה cannot follow רבי עקיבא
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי עקיבא adds אשת אח and אחות אשה to the women who need a גט

steps.title: רב explains רבי עקיבא's brother's-wife case
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that רבי עקיבא's אשת אח case is one where the brother had only betrothed her. People might think that betrothal had a condition and was cancelled, so they would think the second marriage was valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it said about this ברייתא, in the name of רב: what is the brother's-wife case? His brother betrothed a woman and went overseas. He heard his brother died, so he married her (as a יבמה). People will say the first man's betrothal had a condition, and this man married her properly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to reject the proof. It shows that רבי עקיבא's rule was said about a specific kind of case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's reason for requiring a גט is about how things look: people might think the first betrothal was conditional and fell apart. If they see her leave with no גט, they may wrongly think a married woman can leave without one. So the גט is needed because of what onlookers will think, and only when the first bond was just קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it said about it? This introduces a known explanation that weakens the proof.
What is the case? What are the circumstances?
Overseas, a faraway place
A condition attached to a betrothal
Because people will say

phrases.english: But wasn't it said about it,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב גִּידֵּל אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Giddel said Rav Ḥiyya bar Yosef said Rav said:
this brother's wife, what is the case?
For example, his brother betrothed a woman,
and went overseas,
and he heard that his brother died,
and he went and married his wife,
phrases.notes: 'His wife' means the brother's wife. He married her as a יבמה, thinking his brother had died.

phrases.english: because people will say:

phrases.aramaic: הָךְ קַמָּא, תְּנָאָה הֲוָה לֵיהּ בְּקִידּוּשִׁין,
phrases.english: that first one had a condition in the betrothal,
and this one married properly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins rejecting step 6's proof by narrowing what case רבי עקיבא meant.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Limits רבי עקיבא's rule to cases where the first bond was only betrothal
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed רבי עקיבא's גט rule applies to every case, including a full marriage

steps.title: רב explains the wife's-sister case the same way
steps.stepSummary: The אחות אשה case is also one where he had only betrothed the first woman. People may think that betrothal was conditional, so the marriage to the sister looks valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this wife's-sister case, what is it? He betrothed a woman, she went overseas, and he heard she died, so he married her sister. People will say the first betrothal had a condition, and this one he married properly.
steps.whatsHappening: רב continues and explains רבי עקיבא's second case, the wife's sister, in the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again the first woman was only betrothed. So people can imagine her betrothal fell apart because of a condition, which makes the sister look like a real wife. This is why רבי עקיבא requires a גט here too.

keyTerms.meaning: A wife's sister, forbidden while the wife is alive
He married properly, a valid marriage

phrases.aramaic: וְהַאי אֲחוֹת אִשָּׁה נָמֵי הֵיכִי דָּמֵי —
phrases.english: And this wife's sister too, what is the case?
For example, he betrothed a woman,
and she went overseas,
and he heard that she died,
so he went and married her sister.
Because people will say:

phrases.aramaic: הָךְ קַמַּיְיתָא, תְּנָאֵי הֲוָה לֵיהּ בְּקִדּוּשֶׁיהָ,
phrases.english: that first one, he had a condition in her betrothal,
and this one he married properly.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַאי אֲחוֹת אִשָּׁה נָמֵי הֵיכִי דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same betrothal-only explanation to the אחות אשה case, which is the one that matters for our משנה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Limits the אחות אשה rule to a first woman who was only betrothed
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Our משנה's case is different from רבי עקיבא's case

steps.title: A full marriage is not assumed to have a condition
steps.stepSummary: In our משנה the first woman was fully married. Nobody will say a full marriage had a condition, so even רבי עקיבא would not require a גט. The משנה can follow רבי עקיבא after all.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a full marriage: can anyone say he had a condition in the marriage?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the rejection. Our משנה involves a full marriage, so רבי עקיבא's reason does not apply to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's גט is only needed because people might imagine a condition cancelled the first bond. With נשואין, people do not imagine that, so no one will think the sister is really his wife. No גט is needed, the real wife is not 'his divorcée's sister,' and our משנה fits רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Full marriage, after the betrothal
Can one really say? A question that expects the answer no.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא requires a גט for an אחות אשה only when the first wife was merely betrothed, because people may think that betrothal was conditional. With a full marriage, as in our משנה, no גט is needed, so the משנה can follow רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: But a full marriage,
phrases.notes: This is our משנה's case, where he had actually married the first wife.

phrases.english: can one say
that he had a condition in the marriage?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the contrast between betrothal (steps 7-8) and full marriage, which completes the rejection of step 6's proof.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Our משנה deals with a full marriage, so even רבי עקיבא does not require a גט from the sister, and the משנה can follow him.

steps.title: רב אשי asks why the משנה leaves out the mother-in-law
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks רב כהנא: if our משנה follows רבי עקיבא, it should also teach the case of חמותו. רבי עקיבא holds that after the wife's death, relations with the mother-in-law are not punished with שריפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to רב כהנא: if this is רבי עקיבא, let him also teach his mother-in-law. We have heard רבי עקיבא say that his mother-in-law after his wife's death is not punished with burning.
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge opens. רב אשי questions whether our משנה really matches רבי עקיבא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא holds that the mother-in-law's prohibition becomes weaker after the wife dies, since there is no שריפה. So, like the brother's wife and the wife's sister, she seems to fit the kind of case he adds. If our משנה follows him, why doesn't it teach her case too?

keyTerms.meaning: Let him also teach. This asks why something was left out.
His mother-in-law
After death, here meaning after his wife's death
Death by burning, the punishment for relations with a mother-in-law

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְרַב כָּהֲנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Rav Kahana:

phrases.aramaic: אִי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, לִיתְנֵי נָמֵי חֲמוֹתוֹ.
phrases.english: If it is Rabbi Akiva, let him also teach his mother-in-law.

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָא שָׁמְעִינַן לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, דְּאָמַר:
phrases.english: For we have heard Rabbi Akiva say:
his mother-in-law after death is not by burning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְרַב כָּהֲנָא: אִי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, לִיתְנֵי נָמֵי חֲמוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns back to the ברייתא from step 6 and challenges its link to רבי עקיבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the ברייתא's list follows רבי עקיבא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי עקיבא holds that the mother-in-law's prohibition weakens after the wife's death, so she should be on his list too. Her absence suggests the list is incomplete or is not his.

steps.title: The source: רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא argue over 'him and them'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא on the פסוק about a man who takes a woman and her mother. רבי ישמעאל reads it as 'him and one of them.' רבי עקיבא reads it as 'him and both of them.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'They shall burn in fire him and them.' This means him and one of them, says רבי ישמעאל. רבי עקיבא says: him and both of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for what step 10 said about רבי עקיבא's view of the mother-in-law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק talks about a man who takes a woman and her mother, and says 'them' will be burned. רבי ישמעאל says only one of the women is meant, since the first wife did nothing wrong. רבי עקיבא says 'both of them,' and the next steps explain what that means.

keyTerms.meaning: Death by burning, one of the four deaths given by בית דין
'Him and them', the words of the פסוק being explained
Both of them
'The words of', meaning this is the opinion of

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:
"They shall burn in fire him and them"
Him and one of them,
these are the words of רבי ישמעאל.
רבי עקיבא says:
Him and both of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the claim inside step 10's question.
steps.raayaObject: רבי עקיבא's view of relations with חמותו after the wife's death
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא on ויקרא 20:14 where רבי עקיבא says 'him and both of them'

steps.title: According to אביי, the dispute is only about how to read the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: אביי says רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא agree on the הלכה and only argue about how to read the פסוק. One sees 'one woman' in it, the other sees 'two.' That explanation causes no problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, according to אביי, who said they only argue about how the פסוק is read: רבי ישמעאל holds it speaks of one woman, and רבי עקיבא holds it speaks of two. That is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the 'granted' half of a question. The גמרא shows אביי's explanation causes no trouble, and this sets up the problem for רבא in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the argument is only about reading the פסוק, then רבי עקיבא never said the mother-in-law's prohibition ends when the wife dies. So there is no reason to add חמותו to the list, and step 10's question goes away.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Granted', the opening of a 'this works, but that doesn't' question
How the meaning of the פסוק is read
That is the difference between them
Fine, it works

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think that under אביי's reading רבי עקיבא holds the mother-in-law's prohibition ends when the wife dies. Both sides agree on the הלכה; they only argue about how the פסוק teaches it.

phrases.english: Granted, according to אביי, who said
the difference between them is how the meaning of the פסוק is read,
that רבי ישמעאל holds: it is written about one,
and רבי עקיבא holds: it is written about two.
That is fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts to judge step 10's question by looking at אביי's explanation of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 10's assumption about רבי עקיבא's view
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This is only the setup. Under אביי there is no difficulty, which points to where the real difficulty will be.

steps.title: According to רבא, חמותו should be on the list
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the real difference is a mother-in-law after the wife dies. Then רבי עקיבא's list should also include חמותו.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבא, who said the difference between them is a mother-in-law after the wife's death, let the list also include his mother-in-law!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives the real question. Under רבא's explanation, the list that follows רבי עקיבא seems to be missing חמותו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא says רבי עקיבא's 'both of them' means burning applies only while both women are alive. After the wife dies, the mother-in-law is no longer punished with שריפה. So she seems to be a woman who could later look allowed to him, like the others on the list, and should need a גט too.

keyTerms.meaning: His mother-in-law
After death, here meaning after his wife has died
'Let it also teach', a question asking why something is missing from a list

phrases.english: But according to רבא, who said:
the difference between them is one's mother-in-law after the wife's death,
let it also teach his mother-in-law!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second half of the 'granted' question. אביי's explanation worked, but רבא's seems to bring back step 10's problem.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's list of women who need a גט (the ברייתא in step 6), which leaves out חמותו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רבא, רבי עקיבא holds the mother-in-law is not punished with burning after the wife dies. So she should be listed with the other women who need a גט, and she is not.

steps.title: No punishment does not mean no prohibition
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק may remove the punishment of burning, but it never removes the איסור. The mother-in-law stays forbidden even after the wife dies, so she is not on the list.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Granted that the פסוק excluded her from burning, did the פסוק exclude her from the prohibition?
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא answers רב אשי's question. Losing the punishment of שריפה does not make the mother-in-law allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even by רבא's reading, רבי עקיבא only takes away the death penalty. The איסור to marry her stays. So she can never become allowed to him, unlike the women on the list, and she does not need a גט.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Granted', admitting one point before limiting it
The פסוק excluded her
A prohibition, even without the death penalty

steps.whatToRemember: A פסוק can take away a punishment without taking away the איסור. Under רבא, רבי עקיבא only removes the שריפה for חמותו after the wife dies. She stays forbidden, so she is not on the list of women who need a גט.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea that a punishment and a prohibition are separate comes up all over the גמרא. Taking away one does not take away the other.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רב כהנא answering רב אשי's question from step 10.

phrases.english: Granted that the פסוק excluded her from burning,
did the פסוק exclude her from the prohibition?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of steps 10 and 13 under רבא's explanation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Separating the punishment from the prohibition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the mother-in-law is not punished with burning after the wife dies, she might be allowed and should need a גט.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the punishment is gone. The איסור stays, so she does not belong on the list.

steps.title: Should the wife become forbidden through her sister?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the wife is not forbidden to her husband after he had relations with her sister. It compares this to אשה שהלך בעלה למדינת הים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let his wife become forbidden to him because he had relations with her sister. That is just like the woman whose husband went overseas.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rule that the wife stays permitted. It points to a similar case where a mistaken relationship does make a woman forbidden to her husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the case of אשה שהלך בעלה למדינת הים, a woman who had relations with another man by mistake becomes forbidden to her husband. The challenge asks: here too a forbidden relationship happened, with the wife's sister, so why shouldn't the wife become forbidden to her husband the same way?

keyTerms.meaning: And let her become forbidden
Sexual relations, literally 'lying'
Her sister, meaning the wife's sister
Just like, a phrase for comparing to a known case
Overseas, a far-off land

phrases.english: And let her be forbidden through the relations with her sister,
phrases.notes: 'Her' is the man's wife. The relations are his, with her sister.

phrases.english: just as it is with a woman
whose husband went overseas!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתֵאָסֵר בִּשְׁכִיבָה דַּאֲחוֹתָהּ, מִידֵּי דְּהָוֵה אַאִשָּׁה שֶׁהָלַךְ בַּעְלָהּ לִמְדִינַת הַיָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new question from a different angle. It moves on from the חמותו discussion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a man's relations with his wife's sister do not make his wife forbidden to him
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Analogy. A mistaken forbidden relationship makes the wife forbidden in the overseas case, so the same should be true here.

steps.title: The cases are not alike: the wife's own sin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the cases are not comparable. A wife who sins on purpose is forbidden by the Torah, so the רבנן extended this to a mistaken sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not comparable. His wife is forbidden by Torah law if she sinned on purpose, so the רבנן made a decree about her for when she sinned by mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer by explaining why the overseas case is different. This is only the first half of the contrast; the second half, about the wife's sister, continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The decree in the overseas case is built on a Torah איסור. A wife who sins במזיד is forbidden מדאורייתא, so the רבנן added a גזירה for בשוגג. The גמרא is setting up the point that the sister case lacks this Torah base for a decree to build on.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not comparable
On purpose, knowingly
By Torah law
By mistake, unknowingly
The Rabbis made a decree

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the overseas wife is forbidden by the Torah when she sinned by mistake. Only her deliberate sin is a Torah איסור; the mistaken case is a rabbinic decree built on top of it.

phrases.english: It is not comparable:
his wife, who if she sinned on purpose is forbidden by Torah law,
the Rabbis decreed about her even when she sinned by mistake,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 15 by rejecting the comparison.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any forbidden relationship by mistake should make the wife forbidden, just as in the overseas case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The overseas decree rests on a Torah איסור for a deliberate sin. A decree only extends an existing Torah prohibition, so the two cases differ.
